newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel cuts retail price of beer.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel cuts retail price of beer.

text.p: Philippine food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp said on Sunday it was reducing the prices of its top product, beer, in a major move to boost sales and reverse slowing demand.

Under the new posted price which will take effect on Monday, a 320-millilitre bottle of San Miguel beer will retail at nine pesos ($0.34), down by 1.50 pesos from the previous price, a company statement said. A 330-millilitre bottle of San Miguel's Red Horse, a stronger beer, will sell for one peso less at eight pesos, it said, adding the prices of other variants of the two brands would also be cut.

"This is a major strategic initiative that will provide a springboard for future growth, ensuring San Miguel's long-term profitability and competitiveness," said Bienvenido Bautista, president of San Miguel Brewing Philippines.
"By making our products more affordable to the consumers, San Miguel will be able to increase volumes and reverse the slowing demand in the domestic beer market," Bautista added.

The industry has been burdened for the past seven years by higher excise taxes and falling volumes, with San Miguel, the country's largest brewer, feeling the heaviest impact. San Miguel, a blue-chip share on the Philippine bourse, reported in April a recurring first quarter net income of 904 million pesos, 25 percent up on its year-earlier 725 million.
But operating income slumped 37 percent to 1.01 billion pesos because of the impact of higher taxes.

Beer industry sales in 1996 fell 15 percent from the 1990 peak of 201 million cases, each case containing 24 bottles of 320 millilitres. "With our new price structure, we are realigning our brands with our consumers' purchasing power in these value-conscious times," Bautista said. To mitigate the effect of a drop in margins, San Miguel will dramatically reduce costs, the company said. (Conversion $1 = 26.3 pesos)
